name: Frame
first: A modifier that puts a view inside an invisible view of a given size, or of a size between a smallest and a largest, and places the view inside it.

dependsOn.why: A frame is a modifier, which returns a new view around the view it is called on.
dependsOn.whyInExample: `frame(width: 80, height: 40)` returns a new view around the color, as `padding(8)` returns a new view around `city`.

dependsOn.why: A frame takes part in the steps of layout: it proposes a size to the view inside it, and chooses its own.
dependsOn.whyInExample: Line 13 proposes 300 by 200 to the frame, as the renderers propose 300 by 200 on the page of Layout process.

what.is: A frame is a modifier that puts a view inside an invisible view of a given size. `frame(width: 80, height: 40)` makes a view of exactly 80 by 40 points. `frame(maxWidth: 100)` makes a view at most 100 points across, which in the other direction lets the view inside choose.
what.afterExample: The first frame is 80 by 40, whatever it is proposed. The second is proposed 300 by 200, and chooses at most 100 across, and the whole 200 down.
what.problem: Sometimes a view must have a set size, or must not grow past one, such as a picture 80 points wide, or a column of text no wider than 600 points. A frame gives a view that size, without changing the view.
what.how: In the steps of layout, the frame is the parent of the view it holds. A frame with a width and a height chooses that size, and proposes it to the view inside. A frame with a largest width proposes no more than that width to the view inside, and in a direction it gives no size for, passes on the proposal it got.

when.text: Use a fixed frame for a view that must be one size, and a frame with a smallest or a largest size for a view that should grow or shrink only so far.
Don't use a frame to make a view's content bigger. A frame changes the space around the view: a text in a large frame keeps the size of its font.

parts.name: The fixed frame, line 4
parts.text: The modifier `frame(width: 80, height: 40)` returns a view that is always 80 by 40 points. It proposes that size to the color inside it, and the color chooses all of it.

parts.name: The frame with a largest width, line 10
parts.text: The modifier `frame(maxWidth: 100)` returns a view that is never wider than 100 points. It gives no height, so in that direction it passes on the proposal, and the color takes the whole height.

steps.text: Lines 3 and 4 make a color in a frame of 80 by 40, and line 5 makes a renderer for it.
Line 6 asks for the image. The frame chooses 80 by 40, and proposes that size to the color, which takes it. Line 7 prints {{80 40}}.
Lines 9 and 10 make a color in a frame whose largest width is 100. Line 11 makes a renderer for it, and line 13 proposes 300 by 200, the size on line 12.
The frame proposes 100 points across to the color, and the whole 200 points down. The color takes both, and the frame chooses the same, so line 15 prints {{100 200}}.

end.text: The fixed frame chose its own size. The flexible frame chose from the proposal, but no more than its largest width.
